title: Unitary classification of essentially normal operators modulo compacts
statement: For bounded essentially normal \(T_1,T_2\) on separable infinite-dimensional \(H\), determine whether essential spectrum and complementary Fredholm-index function classify unitary equivalence modulo compact operators. The essential-normality hypothesis is reconstructed from the BDF attribution.
status: As of 10 November 2026: answered affirmatively in the BDF setting before this talk; \citet[pp.~58--128]{browndouglasfillmore1973unitary}. The notebook's unrestricted formulation is not the theorem.

title: Involution for elliptic Calogero--Moser systems
statement: For reduced crystallographic root systems with Weyl-orbit couplings, construct a generically independent complete set of commuting integrals for the elliptic Hamiltonian on its regular canonical phase space; retain the free center of mass in the particle \(A\)-model.
status: As of 10 November 2026: affirmative in this scope; \citet[pp.~3--5]{khastgirsasaki2001liouville} is a directly checked proof, first publicly circulated 30 May 2000. This does not certify every arbitrary-\(\varepsilon\) or nonreduced variant in the shorthand table.

title: Integrability of exceptional-root Calogero--Moser systems
statement: For \(G_2,F_4,E_6,E_7,E_8\), determine Liouville integrability of the rational, hyperbolic, trigonometric and untwisted elliptic root potentials with couplings constant on Weyl orbits, away from poles.
status: As of 10 November 2026: affirmative in the stated scope. The group-coupling cases occur in \citet[Theorem~1 and Corollary~1]{olshanetskyperelomov1978radial}; \citet[pp.~3--5]{khastgirsasaki2001liouville} supplies the checked general involution argument. Harmonic confinement is not included in that elliptic theorem.

title: Adequate inverse data for Calogero--Moser particle systems
statement: Identify data sufficient to recover a regular particle trajectory, with center-of-mass and permutation conventions fixed. The trace-only wording in the notebook is underdetermined; a concrete corrected rational problem uses the full initial matrices \(Q_0,L_0\).
status: As of 10 November 2026: the rational initial-value reconstruction is explicit by diagonalizing \(Q_0+tL_0\), or its harmonic counterpart. These formulas are read in \citet[Sections~2--3]{sasaki2006explicit}. Traces alone still do not determine matrix entries or a phase point.

title: Involution of the periodic Toda integrals
statement: For the periodic \(n\)-particle Toda Hamiltonian, exhibit \(n\) generically independent conserved functions that commute for the canonical Poisson bracket, keeping the free center-of-mass degree of freedom.
status: As of 10 November 2026: established. \citet[pp.~1668--1669]{kawasaki1976involution}, published 1 May 1976, is a verified publisher record devoted to the claim. Its proof and the earliest-priority chronology were not independently read in this check.

title: Recursive construction of KdV Lax operators
statement: Construct odd differential operators from formal fractional powers of the Schrödinger operator so that their commutators with it have order zero, and organize the resulting compatible higher KdV flows.
status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the formal differential-algebra setting; \citet[Sections~8--12]{gelfanddikii1976fractional} provides the systematic formulation. Formal fractional powers are distinguished from spectral functional calculus.

title: Finite-gap spectra and stationary KdV characterization
statement: Relate real smooth periodic Schrödinger potentials with finitely many open gaps to stationary equations in the KdV hierarchy; the present occurrence is the third-order, at-most-one-gap case.
status: As of 10 November 2026: the periodic stationary-to-finite-gap implication is read in \citet[Section~2, Theorem~2.1]{novikov1974periodic}. The one-gap specialization requires the lower-flow constant and allowance for degenerations; the older general problem's full occurrence list belongs to the cumulative index.

title: Matrix finite-gap inverse problem at fixed spectral curve
statement: Classify the regular rank-one matrix pencils \(D+U-EA\), with fixed distinct diagonal entries of \(A\), whose stationary spectral polynomial is a fixed smooth curve, and distinguish framed potentials from their diagonal-gauge quotient.
status: As of November 2026, solved on the regular algebraic-geometric locus by the Jacobian construction announced here and published in 1976--1977. Related scalar precursors are 1974-336.15 and 1974-340.8; their differently quantified problems are not merged.

title: Continuum confinement and the static potential
statement: For zero-temperature four-dimensional pure \(SU(N)\) Yang--Mills theory with \(N\ge2\), construct a continuum infinite-volume theory and its renormalized external-fundamental-charge observable, and prove a positive asymptotic string tension \(\lim_{R\to\infty}V(R)/R>0\). The notes motivate this statement but leave its matter-content, phase and continuum/regularization qualifications implicit; the formal action already has \(d^4x\).
status: As of November 2026, the four-dimensional continuum statement is unresolved. Wilson's 1974 fixed-lattice strong-coupling construction is a prior partial realization, and the existence/mass-gap problem is logically distinct. Record 386 supplies a related Hamiltonian observable, to be linked at integration.

title: Monotone radial profile from the indexed frequency matrix
statement: Recover the positive radial coefficient \(f\) of \(y^{\prime\prime}+[\lambda_{k\ell}^2f^2-\ell(\ell+1)/r^2]y=0\), with regular origin and fixed separated outer boundary condition, from its fully indexed spectrum, assuming \(rf\) is strictly increasing and normalized at the outer radius.
status: As of November 2026, the reported monotone reconstruction is identified with Brodskii1976, Theorems1–2; its Abel inversion is classical. The accompanying necessary spectral compatibility condition is not advertised as a full characterization of exact arrays.

title: Rank-one pointed-curve inverse correspondence
statement: For a fixed smooth pointed projective complex curve and local parameter, classify rank-one Krichever homomorphisms from its punctured-curve function ring to ordinary differential operators with smooth germ coefficients, modulo unit scalar gauge, including the unit leading-coefficient germ as data.
status: As of November 2026, the precise local correspondence is established: an acyclic degree-(g-1) initial line bundle and a unit leading coefficient determine the homomorphism. Drinfeld1977, Corollary2, gives the statement and attributes it to Krichever. This is distinct from the later higher-rank inverse problem.

title: Commuting scalar operators of orders two and three
statement: Find smooth local coefficients \(u,v_1,v_2\) for which \([-D^2+u,D^3+v_1D+v_2]=0\), including degenerations of the elliptic solutions.
status: As of November 2026, this is a classical solved problem, already treated in the early commuting-operator literature. It is related to GP-1974-10 (finite-gap/stationary-KdV characterization), whose broader spectral quantifiers are not merged with this exact exercise.

title: Normalization of the generalized Poisson law
statement: For \(x_0>0\) and \(0\le\alpha<1\), prove that \(P_0=e^{-x_0}\), \(P_n=e^{-x_0-\alpha n}x_0(x_0+\alpha n)^{n-1}/n!\) have total mass one.
status: Solved before the meeting in the generalized Poisson literature (1973); the occurrence includes an elementary generating-function reconstruction. Status checked November 2026.

title: Deforming a superfunction algebra along an even Poisson bracket
statement: Construct a formal associative superproduct whose first graded commutator is a given even super-Poisson bracket. The notebook leaves the geometric and parity hypotheses unspecified; the definite version treated here is the Rothstein bracket on a split supermanifold over a symplectic base.
status: The specified symplectic version has a Fedosov-type construction, circulated in 2000. This is a partial identification of the notebook question, not a claim about arbitrary odd or degenerate brackets. Status November 2026.

title: Reconstructing higher-rank commuting ordinary differential operators
statement: Recover a commutative ring of scalar ordinary differential operators from generic pointed spectral-curve and rank-\(r\) bundle data, with the framing and functional parameters required at infinity; orders four and six are the recorded motivating example.
status: The generic smooth-curve inverse construction was completed in Krichever’s article submitted in February 1977 and published in 1978, with corrections to the preceding implementation. Status November 2026.

title: Abel limits of Laplace spectral phases
statement: Let \((M,g)\) be a closed compact Riemannian manifold, let \(\lambda_k\ge0\) be the eigenvalues of \(\sqrt{-\Delta_g}\), counted with multiplicity, and let \(a>0\). Determine when \(\varepsilon\sum_ke^{-\varepsilon\lambda_k}(\delta_{\rm per}(\mu-a\lambda_k)-(2\pi)^{-1})\) converges as a periodic distribution, and express its nonzero Fourier coefficients through closed geodesics. The source’s intended genericity assumptions are incomplete. The intended geometric setting has isolated closed geodesics and pairwise incommensurable primitive unoriented lengths; nondegeneracy of contributing iterates is supplied as a modern trace-formula hypothesis, not a certain reading of an abbreviation.
status: As of November 2026, fixed-mode closed-orbit contributions are explained by wave-trace theory. A source proving the full distributional limit under exactly the notebook’s hypotheses was not located; uniform growth and noncancellation are the explicit remaining qualifications, not an assertion that the whole wave-trace problem is open. The chapter develops the Fourier convergence criterion and solves the circle model; its sphere counterexample explicitly lies outside those geometric hypotheses.

title: A Harnack-type bound for sums of eigenfunctions
statement: The definite reconstructed question is whether the extended Courant nodal-domain bound holds for linear combinations of Laplace eigenfunctions below an eigenvalue cutoff. Arnold’s notebook intervention asks more broadly for a Harnack-type extension and states no exact bound.
status: The specified extended Courant property is false in general; an explicit two-dimensional Neumann counterexample is given in the 2018 paper. This is a partial match to the broader historical question. Status November 2026.

title: Infinitely many nonzero coefficients in Perchik’s relative Euler series
statement: For the fixed-rank plane Hamiltonian Lie algebra, determine whether the relative Euler coefficients \(E_m=\chi H^*(\mathfrak{ham}_2,\mathfrak{sp}_2)_{2m}\) are nonzero for infinitely many positive integers \(m\). The series includes the linear Hamiltonians and is not the series for \(\mathfrak{ham}_2^0\).
status: No resolution was located as of 10 November 2026. The bounded development derives the product rigorously and verifies all coefficients through m=150 by two independent exact methods; this does not prove infinitude.

title: Full cohomology of formal Hamiltonian vector fields
statement: Compute the continuous cohomology of \(\mathfrak{ham}_{2n}\), already for \(n=1\), with its grading and products. This is distinct from the solved cohomology calculation for the full formal-vector-field algebra \(W_n\).
status: Finite-weight classes and factorizations are established, but the targeted search through 10 November 2026 located no complete fixed-rank answer. Stable-rank graph-homology calculations are not a solution of this fixed-rank problem.

title: Serre’s problem for polynomial rings
statement: Is every finitely generated projective module over a polynomial ring over a field free? The earlier three-variable instance recurs in arbitrary dimension, together with unimodular-row completion.
status: Quillen and Suslin solved the problem in 1976. Their manuscripts were received before the April seminar, but receipt does not establish public circulation. Suslin's Section III, Theorems 2--3, and Quillen's publisher chronology were checked. Status November 2026.
